plan.contextChunk: This figure is a shaded perspective drawing of a clear cylindrical container partly filled with a pale blue liquid. The vessel has an elliptical rim with a thick rounded glass lip, a slightly darker band marking the liquid surface a short way down, and a darker pooled region across the curved bottom. Three small cubes outlined in black dashed lines sit at different places within the liquid, each drawn in the container's perspective and each carrying a numeral: cube 1 high and toward the left, cube 2 a little lower and to the right, and cube 3 near the bottom center. A curved arrow links each cube to its own label, written as a ratio in tall parentheses with a subscript, reading Δm/ΔV with subscript 1 at the upper right, Δm/ΔV with subscript 2 at the middle right, and Δm/ΔV with subscript 3 out to the left. Giving each sampling cube its own subscripted mass-to-volume ratio invites the reader to treat the three as separate numbers rather than one value for the whole vessel, which is how local density is defined point by point.

pale blue translucent liquid filling the lower ~75% of the cylinder
slightly darker elliptical liquid surface band a short way below the rim
darker pooled blue region along the curved bottom interior
cube 1: small black dashed-outline cube high and toward the left inside the liquid, numeral 1
cube 2: small black dashed-outline cube slightly lower and to the right, numeral 2
cube 3: small black dashed-outline cube near the bottom center, numeral 3
curved leader arrows from each cube to its label
label (Δm/ΔV)₁ upper right, (Δm/ΔV)₂ middle right, (Δm/ΔV)₃ out to the left, each in tall parentheses with subscript

interactions.teaches: Selecting one dashed cube highlights it and reveals its own measured Δm/ΔV value, showing that density is evaluated locally at the chosen point rather than globally

interactions.label: Sample volume ΔV
interactions.teaches: Shrinking the sampled volume makes the measured Δm/ΔV settle toward a point value — the density ρ = lim (ΔV→0) Δm/ΔV at that location

interactions.label: Liquid
interactions.teaches: Switching between a uniform liquid (all three ratios equal) and a stratified/heterogeneous one (ratios differ by position) shows when a single bulk density suffices and when local density is position-dependent

demo_steps.title: Heterogeneous liquid, three samples
demo_steps.narration: In the default stratified liquid, the three cubes report different Δm/ΔV values — denser near the bottom (cube 3) than near the top (cube 1).

demo_steps.title: Shrink the sample volume
demo_steps.narration: Slide ΔV down on a selected cube: the measured ratio changes less and less, converging to the local density at that point — the limit behind ρ = Δm/ΔV.

demo_steps.title: Uniform liquid
demo_steps.narration: Switch to a uniform liquid: all three cubes now read the same value regardless of position or sample size — one bulk density describes the whole vessel.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Cylinder: radius ~1.2 units, total height ~3.6 units, centered at origin, +Y up. Liquid fills from y=-1.8 to y=+0.9 (surface ellipse at y=0.9 slightly darker). Glass wall pale grey-cyan, opacity ~0.15; liquid pale blue #bcd7ec opacity ~0.35; darker bottom pool #8fb8dd. Camera at three-quarter view (az ~30°, el ~18°) as in the source. Cubes: dashed black edges, default side 0.5 units (scaled by the slider). Cube 1 at (-0.45, 0.35, 0.1), cube 2 at (0.35, -0.25, 0.2), cube 3 at (0.0, -1.15, 0.15) — matching source positions (1 high-left, 2 mid-right, 3 bottom-center). Each cube gets a curved leader arrow to its label sprite: (Δm/ΔV)₁ upper right of the cylinder, (Δm/ΔV)₂ middle right, (Δm/ΔV)₃ out to the left. Density model: uniform mode ρ = 1.0 everywhere; heterogeneous mode ρ(y) = 1.3 - 0.45*(y+1.8)/2.7 (linear stratification, denser at bottom), so displayed ratio = ρ at cube center, and mass Δm = ρ·ΔV. Show numeric value beside the selected cube's label only (as the source shows symbols, values appear on selection).
interactionPlan.notes: Render cubes as LineSegments with LineDashedMaterial (black) plus a faint fill so clicks register; highlight the selected cube with a warm yellow fill (#ffd54a, opacity 0.5). Labels as CanvasTexture sprites positioned outside the cylinder; only the selected cube's label shows the numeric ratio. Curved arrows via QuadraticBezierCurve3 tubes. Recompute Δm, ΔV and the ratio reactively when the slider or toggle changes. Glass via MeshPhysicalMaterial with transmission or simple transparent Phong material; keep the liquid a separate inner cylinder so the surface ellipse reads clearly.

authoredContext:
The density of a substance is not necessarily constant throughout the volume of a substance. If the density is constant throughout a substance, the substance is said to be a homogeneous substance. A solid iron bar is an example of a homogeneous substance. The density is constant throughout, and the density of any sample of the substance is the same as its average density. If the density of a substance were not constant, the substance is said to be a heterogeneous substance. A chunk of Swiss cheese is an example of a heterogeneous material containing both the solid cheese and gas-filled voids. The density at a specific location within a heterogeneous material is called local density, and is given as a function of location, ρ=ρ(x,y,z) (the figure).

Density may vary throughout a heterogeneous mixture. Local density at a point is obtained from dividing mass by volume in a small volume around a given point.

Figure is a drawing of a container filled with a liquid. Small cubes are drawn in different regions of the container to indicate local density points.

Local density can be obtained by a limiting process, based on the average density in a small volume around the point in question, taking the limit where the size of the volume approaches zero,
